problem: The loop says to solve Rachford-Rice for β between 0 and 1, but no β in (0,1) exists when every Ki is above 1 or every Ki is below 1 (single-phase feed). As written, a student can set up a two-phase flash at 40 bar for a mixture whose K values are all below 1, as in Worked example 1, and get a spurious or non-converging β.
fix: Add the guard: if all Ki > 1 report a single vapour phase (β = 1); if all Ki < 1 report a single liquid phase (β = 0); solve Rachford-Rice only when the K values straddle 1.

where: Section 2 and Section 3 (loop and exam traps)
problem: The phi-phi loop can converge to the trivial solution, where the EOS returns the same root for both phases, giving Ki = 1 for every component and x = y. This is a false convergence, and the chapter never tells the student to test for it.
fix: Add a check: after convergence, reject the result if all Ki are close to 1 and the liquid and vapour roots of Z are (nearly) the same; restart from a different Wilson estimate or a different initial β.

where: Section 3, bubble point and dew point sentences
problem: The bubble point needs a vapour composition to evaluate φiV, and the dew point needs a liquid composition to evaluate φiL, but the text only says solve ΣxiKi = 1 or Σyi/Ki = 1. A student will not know what composition goes into the EOS inside the bubble/dew loop.
fix: State that in the bubble point y is renormalised from y = xK/(ΣxK) after each K update, and in the dew point x is renormalised from x = (y/K)/(Σy/K), and that these normalised compositions are what feed the EOS fugacity coefficients.

problem: Natural gas drying is usually glycol absorption, not a separation whose design rests on the phi-phi flash described here; listing it next to gas separation and absorption is loose.
fix: Say natural gas processing: dew-point control, NGL recovery and high-pressure absorption.
